candidate_relations.reason: AMVC presents with round atrophic scar-like lesions, epidermal dell, dermal fibrosis, and reduced elastic fibers on orcein stain without follicular involvement. Follicular atrophoderma is a related but incompatible subtype characterized by follicular ostia enlargement and ice-pick depressions, typically associated with Bazex syndrome or other genodermatoses. The histopathology here (epidermal dell, lymphocytic infiltrate, elastic fiber reduction) and clinical features (no follicular pattern, bilateral malar/preauricular distribution, no prior inflammation) are characteristic of AMVC, not follicular atrophoderma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Follicular atrophoderma is a distinct subtype of atrophoderma with follicular (ice-pick) pitting pattern, differing from AMVC which features non-follicular round atrophic scars with elastic fiber loss and lymphocytic infiltrate

case_quality_flags: Classic AMVC presentation with pathognomonic orcein stain findings; differential from follicular atrophoderma is histopathologically well-supported
